title: Part Eighteen: Family Policy and the Safety Net

sections.brief: Leave after a birth (NII maternity insurance from 1954; paid weeks 12→14→15 in 2007 and 2017; cap NIS 1,752.33/day 2026; 26 weeks protected; fathers 1,266 in 2018) vs FMLA 1993 unpaid 12 weeks, employer paid leave ~10% (2010) → 27% (2023), 13% vs 44% by wage quartile, ten state programmes; childcare (Israel free preschool 3–4 from 2012, link us14; DOL NDCP $6,552–15,600, 8.9–16% of median income, 2022); child allowance (1959; 2003 and 2013 cuts, 2015 restoration and savings plan; 2026 rates) vs CTC (2021 expansion, SPM child poverty 5.2%→12.4%); OECD family spending (SOCX US 0.77%→0.60% 1980–2023, Israel 1.89% 2023; PF1.1 with tax breaks US <1% vs OECD 2.35%). Figures: compare; stats

Israel's 1977 committee law (grounds, 38 committees, 99.6% of 16,492 approved 2020, half outside committees per 2012 report, state basket since 2014, June 2022 Horowitz reform) vs post-Dobbs US (Hyde since 1977; 13 total bans Jan 2026; #WeCount 1.13m abortions 2025, telehealth 5%→29%); IVF (Israel basket under 45 up to two children, most cycles per capita; US no entitlement, 2025 Trump EO); fertility (Israel TFR 2.93 1990s → 3.08 2015–19 → 2.89 2022; US ~2.1 2007 → 1.599 2024; GFR 53.1 2025). Figures: compare; time

Old-age pensions: Social Security (71m beneficiaries, $1,609.5bn 2025, lifts 28.8m out of SPM poverty; 2026 Trustees: OASI 2032, OASDI 2034, 83% payable, deficit 4.42%) vs NII old-age allowance (~22% replacement, supplement to 24% of elderly; ages 67/62); Israel's 1995 fund closure and 2008 mandatory pension (17.5% from 2014) vs voluntary US plans; disability (Israel 2018 law NIS 4.3bn, to nearly NIS 4,000, 84–0; US DI in OASDI); NII long-term care reform Nov 2018 (309,435 recipients); unemployment not compared (gap stated). Figures: compare

Two definitions (NII relative 50% of median vs US official fixed thresholds and SPM); US official 1959–2025 (22.4% → 10.2% record low; 2024 10.6 vs 10.7 contradiction), SPM 13.1%, 2025 cuts; Israel 2004–2024 with the 2011–12 survey break (23.6/24.5 → ~21.9 → 20.7%), child 28%; OECD-scale comparison (Israel 19.5% vs OECD 11.6%; children 23.4 vs 12.4); transfers (31.5% → 20.7%; income support erosion 71% → 48.9% of line 2002–06); elderly 25.1% 2004 → 12.8% 2023 with method caveat; Arab/Haredi family rates vs family national rate.
